entity_resolution.arabic_name: أبو الريحان محمد بن أحمد البيروني

timeline_a_biological.event: Born in Kath, the capital of the Afrighid dynasty of Khwarazm.
Fled Khwarazm following political upheaval and civil war, moving to Rayy.
Joined the court of Ziyarid ruler Shams al-Ma'ali Qabus in Tabaristan.
Taken to Ghazni by Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni; subsequently traveled throughout the Indian subcontinent.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Constructed an astronomical instrument to measure the solar meridian transit in Kath.
Completed 'The Remaining Signs of Past Centuries' (Kitab al-Athar al-Baqiyah), a foundational work on chronologies and calendars.
Calculated the radius of the Earth using trigonometric dip-angle measurements from a mountain at Nandana Fort.
Authored 'Kitab al-Hind' (Indica) and completed 'Al-Qanun al-Mas'udi', a comprehensive encyclopedia of astronomy and geodesy.
Wrote 'Kitab al-Jamahir fi Ma'rifat al-Jawahir', detailing experimental methods in hydrostatic density measurement.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Geodetic Determination of Earth Radius via Horizon Dip Angle
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Determining the radius and circumference of the Earth accurately without requiring long overland distance measurement surveys across flat land.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: The Earth's radius can be derived by combining the measured height of a mountain with the dip angle of the sea or plain horizon viewed from its peak.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Al-Biruni measured the height of a mountain at Nandana (in modern Pakistan) using two sighting angles on a nearby flat plain. He then climbed to the peak and used an astrolabe to measure the dip angle (the angle between the true horizontal plane and the visual horizon).

variables_definition.h: Height of the mountain above the surrounding plain
variables_definition.\\theta: Dip angle of the horizon below the local horizontal

equations.validity_domain: Macroscopic terrestrial geodesy assuming spherical Earth symmetry.
equations.assumptions: Earth is perfectly spherical; light travels in straight paths; atmospheric refraction near horizon is constant or negligible.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Calculated the Earth's radius to be approximately 6,339.6 km (3,928.7 miles), which is within 1% of modern mean Earth radius values (~6,371 km). This method drastically reduced the physical labor needed for large-scale geographic measurements.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Highly sensitive to errors in measuring the small dip angle \theta and atmospheric refraction variations near the line of sight.

physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Determining the purity and material identity of metals and gemstones by accurately measuring their specific gravity relative to water.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: By designing an overflow hydrostatic vessel (pycnometer prototype) and using precise balance mechanics, relative density can be calculated by measuring the displaced mass of water directly.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Al-Biruni constructed a specialized conical vessel filled with water up to a precise lateral spout. Inserting a solid displaced an exact volume of water through the spout into a receptacle, allowing ratio measurements between the mass of the solid and the mass of equal-volume displaced water.

variables_definition.W_{air}: Weight of the solid sample measured in air
variables_definition.W_{water}: Apparent weight of the solid sample submerged in water

equations.validity_domain: Incompressible non-porous solids and static liquids.
equations.assumptions: Water temperature remains constant; fluids are incompressible; no air bubbles adhere to the submerged sample surface.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Determined the specific gravity of 18 metals and precious stones (e.g., gold = 19.05, mercury = 13.56, iron = 7.82) matching modern values to within 1-2% accuracy, laying foundational techniques for quantitative mineralogy.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Limited by surface tension at the vessel spout and lack of temperature standardization for liquid density.

collaborators: Ibn Sina (Avicenna) [scholarly correspondence on natural philosophy and physics]
